newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: KL interbank rates steady, focus on one-month.
newsitem.headline: KL interbank rates steady, focus on one-month.

text.p: Interbank rates were little changed on Tuesday with early activity confined to bidding by finance companies for one-month money, dealers said.
"There's some interest in the one-month but elsewhere, it's very quiet," said a dealer at a Malaysian bank.
One-week money was at 6.80/90 percent against 6.9/7.0 on Monday, while two-week and three-week were steady at 7.00/10 and 7.10/20 percent respectively.
One-month money at 7.30/35 percent against 7.25/30. Three-month at 7.35/40 percent and six-month at 7.40/45, were both unchanged.
Dealers said they expected rates to hover at current levels with players continuing to await announcement of a new long-term government bond issue.
Speculation has been rife that Bank Negara will issue new Malaysian Government Securities (MGS) to roll over maturing bonds. A 900-million ringgit issue will mature on May 15.
The overnight interbank rate is expected to stay around 7.0 percent ahead of Wednesday's 500 million ringgit payment for a 30-day Bank Negara bill issue, dealers said.
The issue is to roll over maturing bills of the same amount. The maturity is on Friday.
Interest rate futures on the Malaysia Monetary Exchange were also generally steady.
At 0300 GMT, the benchmark three-month Kuala Lumpur Interbank Offered Rate (KLIBOR) December contract was unchanged at 92.69, or an implied yield of 7.31 percent.
March 1998 was steady at 92.64, or 7.34 percent.
